The film begins with wider camera lenses that give its scenes a sense of openness and spatial freedom, and gradually shifts to longer lenses with tighter framing as the film progresses. This technique compressed depth, reduced visible space between characters, and created an increasing sense of psychological pressure and confinement, all without changing the physical setting.
True to his theatre-influenced approach, Y conducted extensive rehearsals with the cast before filming, but avoided rehearsing once the camera rolled, aiming to capture fresh, instinctive performances. The film was shot on a tight schedule of just a few weeks, relying on preparation and precision rather than multiple takes.
